newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: RINGGIT REBOUNDS VS DOLLAR ON PROFIT-TAKING.
newsitem.headline: RINGGIT REBOUNDS VS DOLLAR ON PROFIT-TAKING.

text.p: * Ringgit rebounds on profit-taking after dollar's failure to test higher levels in London
The ringgit rebounded against the dollar as players locked in profits after the dollar's failure to test higher levels in London overnight, dealers said.
"Dollar failed to move above 2.79 in London last night and this triggered the pullback," said a dealer at a Malaysian bank. "There was also a lot of profit-taking above 2.78."
At 0145 GMT, the ringgit was quoted at 2.7590/640 to a dollar, after hitting a low of 2.7880 in London overnight.
Dealers said technical buying and the dollar's retreat against the major currencies also helped the ringgit's recovery.

They said comments by Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad on Wednesday that Malaysia will reduce imports and review plans for some large projects due to a sharp fall in the ringgit against the dollar have also tempered the dollar's bullish tone.
But the downside risk for ringgit was still intact, dealers said.
"We're looking at support for dollar at 2.74-2.75. A move to 2.80 is still on the cards," a dealer with another Malaysian bank said.
Dealers expected another choppy session given the continued thin volumes and wide spreads.
